title: Pathway memory is distributed uniformly across organism classes

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Pathway memory is distributed uniformly across organism classes

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Memory in the surveyed pathway models shows no privileged association with any class of organism (bacteria, slime mould, yeast, plants, lower vertebrates, mammals), being distributed roughly uniformly, which may suggest that proto-cognitive capacity is found across many strata of life.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Learning in Transcriptional Network Models: Computational Discovery of Pathway-Level Memory and Effective Interventions

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Biswas S 2022, Learning in Transcriptional Network Models: Computational Discovery of Pathway-Level Memory and Effective Interventions › 2. Results › 2.5. Can Networks Be Trained to Keep More Than One Memory?

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: We found no privileged categorization of memory over classes of organisms—memory seemed distributed uniformly over all strata of life (see Figure S3).

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Biswas S, Clawson W, Levin M, “Learning in Transcriptional Network Models: Computational Discovery of Pathway-Level Memory and Effective Interventions”, International journal of molecular sciences (2022), doi:10.3390/ijms24010285; section “2. Results › 2.5. Can Networks Be Trained to Keep More Than One Memory?”. Scope: 35 BioModels pathway models grouped by source organism

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2022-grn-learning-13: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.73

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The distribution within the selected survey is easy to recompute. The extrapolation to many strata of life is poorly covered and strongly subject to repository selection bias.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Group the 35 models by source organism class and compare memory prevalence using uncertainty-aware tests. A larger stratified BioModels sample is needed to test uniformity across life rather than merely this survey.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Available models are not a representative sample of organismal strata.

Classes have small and unequal samples.

Some models are general rather than species-specific.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
discriminating power: 0.52
data adequacy: 0.48
analysis feasibility: 0.92
operationalizability: 0.84
data existence: 0.88

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Organism metadata and memory counts are both recoverable, so the distribution inside this list can be rechecked. The list is not a sample of life, and 'roughly uniformly' plus the suggestion about all strata of life outruns what 35 published models can show. The test covers a thin proxy for the stated scope.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Label each of the 35 models by the source taxon class recorded in BioModels and test whether memory prevalence is homogeneous across bacteria, slime mould, yeast, plants, vertebrates and mammals. A clearly uneven distribution would refute uniformity inside this set; a flat distribution would support only that limited census.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Uniformity among published models does not measure proto-cognitive capacity across living taxa.

Class sizes in a 35-model curated list are too small for a uniformity test to be stable.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
analysis feasibility: 0.68
data adequacy: 0.4
operationalizability: 0.65
discriminating power: 0.38
data existence: 0.75
